No military pathway by which Myanmar's civil war threatens Germans' physical safety has been confirmed.
Myanmar is a minor source of energy and food for Germany, so no change in daily life has been confirmed.
Instability in heavy rare earth supplies from Kachin State is an indirect pathway via processing in China, and no change in Germans' daily lives has been observed.
Data counting the number of Germans harmed by scam syndicates in Southeast Asia (from the Foreign Office, the Federal Criminal Police Office, or other sources) would settle this.
The Myanmar civil war has no nuclear pathway.
Refugees from Myanmar remain in neighboring countries such as Thailand, Bangladesh, and India, and no meaningful flow to Germany has been confirmed.
There is no military pathway from the border fighting and airstrikes to Germans' safety.
The two countries account for small shares of global energy and grain supplies, so there is no link to Germany.
Germany's trade with the two countries is small, so there is no pathway to Germans' daily lives.
Militant attacks in this conflict are aimed at targets inside Pakistan, and no pathway to Germany has been confirmed.
Pakistan is nuclear-armed, but its adversary is a non-nuclear regime, and no pathway for nuclear use or leakage of nuclear material has been reported in this conflict.

cells.m: Pressure from Pakistan, at odds with the Taliban government, to expel Afghans → Risk of deportation for Afghans waiting in Islamabad with pledges of admission to Germany, and their transfer to Germany → Costs of Germany's admission program and a domestic political debate
cells.b: In January 2026, Germany flew 32 Afghans from Islamabad to Berlin, and Afghans with pledges of admission to Germany were reported to be at risk of deportation from Pakistan to Taliban-ruled Afghanistan (KabulNow, citing Deutsche Welle, January 10, 2026). Whether Pakistan's expulsions after the declaration of war in February 2026 have strengthened this link, and any change in asylum applications by Afghans in Germany, could not be confirmed.

cells.r: No link by which a military threat from the Strait of Malacca reaches Germans' personal safety has been confirmed.
Germany's energy and food imports do not depend heavily on the Strait of Malacca.

The toll proposal was withdrawn in April, shipping was not disrupted, and no change in container freight rates to Europe has been confirmed, so the verdict is the same as for the Western, Central, and Eastern Europe cell.
No hybrid activity connected to the Strait of Malacca has been confirmed.
The Strait of Malacca has no nuclear pathway.
The toll proposal and piracy in the Strait of Malacca do not cause population movement, and there is no link to movement involving Germany.

cells.m: Russian provocations on NATO's eastern flank and military forces in Kaliningrad and Belarus → The Bundeswehr's 45th Armored Brigade permanently stationed in Lithuania, with compulsory transfers of specialists → Risks to the safety of soldiers and their families and strains on their daily lives
cells.b: Germany keeps its 45th Armored Brigade in Rūdninkai, about 30 kilometers from the Belarusian border, and plans to station about 4,800 troops there permanently by the end of 2027; in September 2026 it decided to transfer personnel compulsorily to specialist posts it could not fill with volunteers (Euronews, September 14, 2026). In May 2026, Russian warships stayed for weeks in the waters between Fehmarn and Rostock, and Germany sent an intelligence-gathering ship to the Baltic Sea (European Pravda, May 28, 2026).

cells.r: The drone sightings over the Kiel power plant and the Heide refinery in September 2025 fall outside the past 12 months, and who was behind them has not been identified; since then, no case has been confirmed in which Baltic Sea tensions damaged German energy facilities or disrupted supplies.

Poland's closure of its border with Belarus (September 2025) falls outside the past 12 months, and no source confirms the effect of disruptions to China-EU rail freight on German logistics and import companies.

cells.m: Satellite navigation (GPS) interference from the Kaliningrad area and Russian shadow fleet operations in the Baltic Sea → Disrupted positioning data for aircraft over northeastern Germany and maritime safety risks off the German coast
cells.b: In April 2024, Germany's Defense Ministry said GPS interference in the Baltic Sea very likely originated in Russia and named Kaliningrad as its source (The Baltic Times), and Germany's air navigation service provider (DFS) received 447 reports of GPS interference from January to August 2025 (FTN News). The Defense Ministry said in May 2026 that Russian warships had been deployed off the German coast to prevent inspections of shadow fleet tankers (European Pravda, May 28, 2026). No tally of harm to Germany in the past 12 months could be confirmed.

cells.m: Warnings of nuclear use if Kaliningrad is blockaded → A heightened sense of nuclear threat among Germans, whose country is a NATO member with troops near Kaliningrad
cells.b: On September 30, 2026, Russia warned NATO members in a diplomatic note that if Kaliningrad were blockaded, it could use all weapons, including nuclear weapons (Al Jazeera). Germany was not singled out in the warning, and no actual change in Germans' daily lives (such as civil defense measures) could be confirmed.

cells.m: Migrant arrivals via Belarus → Secondary movement through Latvia, Lithuania, and Poland toward Germany → Poland's extended checks at its border with Germany, delays at German-Polish border crossings, and disputes over border policy
cells.b: Lithuania's State Border Guard Service said 1,288 migrants entering Latvia from Belarus were caught in 2025 (540 the year before), and that migrants heading for Western Europe mainly passed through Lithuania and Poland with Germany as their destination (European Pravda, January 6, 2026). On October 1, 2026, Poland extended temporary checks at its borders with Germany and Lithuania until March 30, 2027, and since introducing them it has refused entry to about 1,200 people at the German border (Internazionale, citing Reuters). The Polish government's announcement cited illegal migration as the reason for the checks and did not mention Belarus directly.

cells.m: Russian airstrikes on Ukraine's Danube ports → Drones crossing into Romanian airspace → Scrambles by German Air Force fighters stationed at Romania's Mihail Kogălniceanu base, with risks and strain for the personnel
cells.b: On February 26, 2026, German and Spanish Eurofighters scrambled from Romania's Mihail Kogălniceanu base in response to a drone that had briefly entered Romanian airspace north of Sulina; there were no casualties or damage (Army Recognition).

cells.r: No effect of the drone incursions on Germany's energy or food supply has been observed.
Changes in cargo volumes at the Danube delta and Romanian ports concern Romania, and no change in German trade has been confirmed.

The plans Prime Minister Donald Tusk disclosed for hybrid attacks on countries supporting Ukraine are the same link as at the Russia-Ukraine war flashpoint, and the actual case in Germany (the explosive drone at Leipzig/Halle Airport) is covered under that flashpoint. No separate link from incursions into Romanian airspace to Germany has been confirmed.
Incidents at this flashpoint are conventional drone and missile incursions, with no nuclear dimension.
Ukrainian refugees in Germany are a result of the Russia-Ukraine war as a whole, and no new refugee flow arising from drone incursions along the Danube border has been confirmed.
No military link threatening Germans' personal safety has been confirmed in connection with the Greenland issue.
There is no pathway from the Greenland issue to Germany's energy or food supply.

cells.m: The dispute over Greenland's sovereignty → U.S. threats of retaliatory tariffs on eight European countries, including Germany → German exporters and jobs could come under strain.
cells.b: On January 17, 2026, President Donald Trump announced a 10 percent tariff, starting in February, on goods from eight European countries, including Germany, rising to 25 percent on June 1 (PBS, January 17, 2026), but withdrew it on January 21, before it took effect (Euronews). The U.S.-Denmark-Greenland security agreement signed on September 22 reduced the risk of a recurrence.

cells.r: No information operations or cyber activity targeting Germans in connection with the Greenland issue have been confirmed.
No pathway by which the Greenland issue raises nuclear risk has been identified.
There is no refugee or migration pathway involving Germany linked to the Greenland issue.

cells.m: If tensions in northern Kosovo escalate into armed clashes → Bundeswehr troops deployed with KFOR could be exposed to danger.
cells.b: According to a June 12, 2026, report, the Bundeswehr had 308 of KFOR's 4,657 troops (Periskopi). No new casualties among KFOR troops have been confirmed since the clashes in Zvečan in May 2023.

cells.r: Political instability in the Western Balkans is not connected with Germany's sources of energy or food.

Nothing has been observed to show that the changes of government and separatist moves in Serbia and Bosnia have reduced German companies' local production or trade, and these countries account for a small share of German trade, so no link to daily life has been confirmed.
No hybrid activity targeting Germans has been confirmed in the Western Balkans conflict.
The Western Balkans conflict has no nuclear threat pathway.

Migration from the Western Balkans to Germany stems from labor migration programs and economic conditions in the countries of origin, and nothing has been observed to show that political instability around the current elections has changed the flow to Germany or border controls.

cells.m: An explosive drone near an airport, apparently targeting Ukraine-bound transport aircraft → Residents and travelers around German airports and logistics hubs could face risks to their personal safety.
cells.b: In August 2026, an explosive drone apparently targeting Ukraine-bound transport aircraft and one other drone were found near Leipzig/Halle Airport, and in early September Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul and Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt publicly named Russia as responsible (The Christian Science Monitor, September 3, 2026).

cells.r: No case could be found in the past 12 months of an attack on German energy facilities confirmed as the work of Russia or Iran. The January 2026 arson attack on power transmission facilities that caused a blackout in southwestern Berlin drew a statement in the name of the far-left group Vulkangruppe, and no state involvement has been confirmed. The hacking of a British power plant is confined to Britain.
No case of hybrid attacks cutting off Germany's trade or technology flows has been confirmed.

cells.m: Russian drone operations around airports and sabotage → A vicious cycle of insecure infrastructure and diplomatic retaliation against Russia → German society could face growing strain on public safety and politics.
cells.b: In early September 2026, the German government publicly named Russia as responsible for the explosive drone incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport and condemned it as open hostility, and Russia responded by closing the Goethe-Institut's branch in Russia (The Christian Science Monitor, September 3, 2026).

cells.r: No nuclear pathway has been identified in these hybrid attacks.

Russia and Belarus's use of migrants on the Belarus-Poland route is confirmed, but statistics from Germany's Federal Police or BAMF showing how many people entered by this route and applied for asylum in Germany would settle this. Checks at the German-Polish border on the same route are covered under the Baltic Sea and Kaliningrad flashpoint.
There is no military link from regime change in Venezuela to Germans' safety.
Venezuelan crude goes mainly to the United States and accounts for a small share of Germany's crude imports, so no link to energy supply has been confirmed.
Trade between Germany and Venezuela is small, so no trade link to daily life has been confirmed.
No information operations or cyber activity targeting Germans in connection with the regime change have been confirmed.
Venezuela's regime change has no nuclear pathway.
The main destination for Venezuelans heading to Europe is Spain, and no sizable movement to Germany has been confirmed.
The strikes on drug boats are confined to the Caribbean and the eastern Pacific, and there is no link to Germans' safety.
No effect of this operation on Germany's energy or food supply has been observed.
No disruption to Germany's trade or technology related to this operation has been observed.
The strikes are an open military operation, and there are no data showing that they have changed drug smuggling flows to Germany.
This operation has no nuclear dimension.
The strikes on drug boats have no link to population movement involving Germany.
No military pathway by which the Cuba blockade threatens Germans' physical safety has been confirmed.
No effect of the Cuba blockade on Germany's energy or food prices has been confirmed.
Trade between Germany and Cuba is small, so no trade pathway to daily life has been confirmed.
No information warfare or cyber activity targeting Germans in connection with the Cuba crisis has been confirmed.
The Cuba blockade has no nuclear pathway.
Cuban migration to Europe goes mainly to Spain, and no sizable link to Germany has been confirmed.
There is no link from the cartels and the militarization of the border to Germans' safety.
No case or specific link has been confirmed in which cartel and border problems have unsettled Germany's energy or food supply.
Some German automakers have plants in Mexico, but no data could be found showing that U.S. measures against Mexico taken on cartel grounds have changed production or employment at these companies.
Cartel trafficking and drone activity are concentrated on the U.S.-Mexico border and do not target Germans.
The cartel and border problem has no nuclear channel.
Changes in movement across the U.S.-Mexico border have no link to Germany.
The port dispute is being pursued through legal and commercial means, and no threat of force has been found.
Shipping through the canal itself has continued without disruption, so no effect on energy or food shipments to Germany has been confirmed.
Nothing has been observed to show that the dispute over port operating rights has changed canal traffic or the freight rates or delivery times for German cargo.
No hybrid activity targeting Germans related to the Panama port dispute has been confirmed.
The Panama port dispute has no nuclear channel.
The dispute over port operating rights has no channel related to the movement of people.
There is no military pathway from Haiti's gang crisis to Germans' safety.
Haiti is not a source of energy or food for Germany.
Trade between Germany and Haiti is small, so there is no pathway to daily life.
No hybrid activity targeting Germans has been confirmed.
There is no nuclear element.
Haitians move to the Americas and France (including its overseas territories), and no sizable movement to Germany has been confirmed.
As a trade dispute, it involves no military threat.
There is no link from U.S. and Canadian measures on dairy products and alcohol to Germany's food or energy supply.
There are no data showing that U.S.-Canadian tariffs have meaningfully changed Germans' daily lives.
There are no data on hybrid activity targeting Germans.
As a trade dispute, it has no nuclear dimension.
There has been no case of the trade dispute creating or blocking population movement involving Germany.
No military pathway by which gang violence in Ecuador threatens Germans' physical safety has been confirmed.
No case of gang violence disrupting Germany's food imports, such as bananas from Ecuador, has been confirmed.
No change in Germany's trade or supply chains from the deterioration of security in Ecuador has been confirmed.

cells.m: Cocaine smuggled through Ecuadorian ports → Shipments into German ports such as Hamburg → Drug crime and health harms in Germany could grow.
cells.b: In mid-March 2026, 1.6 metric tons of cocaine hidden in several containers from Ecuador were seized at the port of Hamburg (FreshPlaza, April 13, 2026). According to Hamburg's customs investigation office, cocaine seizures at northern German ports in 2025 totaled about 5.1 metric tons (3.6 in Hamburg and 1.5 in Bremerhaven), down from 9.2 metric tons in 2024, and smuggling groups are shifting to smaller ports such as Wilhelmshaven and Emden (Transport Online, May 20, 2026). Ecuador's share of the volume entering Germany could not be confirmed, so confidence is rated medium.

cells.r: Ecuador's gang violence has no nuclear channel.
No meaningful migration flow from Ecuador to Germany has been confirmed.
The front lines are confined to Sudan and neighboring countries, so there is no military pathway to Germans' safety.
Sudan accounts for a small share of global energy and grain supplies, so there is no link to Germany.
Trade between Germany and Sudan is small, so there is no pathway to daily life.
No hybrid activity targeting Germans has been confirmed.
Sudan's civil war has no nuclear channel.

According to the EU Agency for Asylum, of about 31,000 asylum applications by Sudanese in the EU+ from March 2025 to August 2026, Greece (13,000) and France (11,000) accounted for more than three-quarters, and no figure for Germany is given. The number of asylum applications by Sudanese in Germany over the same period and their trend would settle this.
The Bundeswehr withdrew from Mali at the end of 2023 and from Niger in 2024, and JNIM's activity is concentrated within the Sahel, so no attacks on Germans have been confirmed.
The Sahel is not a source of energy or food for Germany, and Niger's nationalization of uranium has no link to Germany.
Germany's trade and technology are not meaningfully connected to the Sahel conflict.
Information warfare in the Sahel targets people in the Sahel, and no case affecting Germans' daily lives has been confirmed.
There is no nuclear-related pathway for Germany linked to the Sahel conflict.

Arrivals in Europe from Mali and elsewhere in the Sahel are concentrated in Spain (the Canary Islands), and no data could be found showing secondary movement on to Germany, so no specific link to Germany has been confirmed.
There is no pathway from the fighting in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to Germans' personal safety.
This flashpoint is not a source of energy or food for Germany.
There is a supply chain pathway through minerals such as coltan, but nothing has been observed to show that this conflict has changed prices of German products or employment.
No hybrid activity targeting Germans has been confirmed.
There is no nuclear pathway.

Asylum seekers in Europe from the Democratic Republic of the Congo concentrate in French-speaking countries such as France and Belgium, and there are no data showing that the flow to Germany has grown since the fighting in the east.
There is no military threat pathway to Germans.
Any effect on Germany would come through the Red Sea route, and the fighting has not reached the Red Sea coast, so no link to energy or food supply has been confirmed.
No disruption to Red Sea shipping has been observed, and the fighting has not reached Eritrea's Red Sea coast (Assab), so any link to German trade is only hypothetical.
There are no data on hybrid activity targeting Germans.
This conflict has no nuclear dimension.

Germany is one of the main destinations for asylum seekers from Eritrea, but monthly BAMF statistics showing whether asylum applications in Germany by Eritreans and Ethiopians have changed since the war resumed on September 22, 2026, would settle this.

cells.m: Participation in the EU's Red Sea escort operation (Aspides) → German naval personnel deployed there could be exposed to Houthi attacks.
cells.b: On October 15, 2026, the Bundestag extended Germany's participation in Operation Aspides to the end of October 2027 and approved the deployment of up to 350 Bundeswehr personnel (Bundestag, October 15, 2026). Whether German warships are actually deployed at present could not be confirmed.

cells.m: Shipping risks in the Red Sea → Disrupted shipments of crude via Yanbu and Suez (SUMED) and of petroleum products from the Middle East and India → Germans could face higher fuel prices through the European market.
cells.b: The crude route to Europe from Yanbu through Suez and SUMED depends on navigation in the northern Red Sea, and tankers leaving Yanbu have been attacked (AGBI, September 2026). According to Germany's Federal Statistical Office, however, the Middle East supplied only 6.1 percent of Germany's crude imports in 2025 and Saudi Arabia only 0.8 percent, so direct dependence is small, and the actual effect on German fuel prices could not be confirmed.

cells.m: Disruptions on the Red Sea and Suez route → Germany-bound containers from Asia diverting around the Cape of Good Hope, with delays and higher costs → Import prices and parts procurement for German manufacturers could come under strain.
cells.b: As of September 2026, most container ships were still diverting around the Cape of Good Hope, and only some services had made a limited return to Suez (AGBI, September 2026). The size of the effect on German companies' logistics costs and delivery times could not be confirmed.

cells.r: No hybrid activity targeting Germans has been confirmed in this conflict. The cutting of undersea cables in the Red Sea in September 2025 falls outside the past 12 months and has not been confirmed as a deliberate attack.
The Red Sea front has no nuclear channel.
No sizable pathway for refugees from Yemen to Germany has been confirmed.
The pathway from threats to the canal and ports to Germans' physical safety is negligible (personal risks to seafarers are a separate matter).

cells.m: Disrupted supplies of crude and jet fuel via Suez → Higher prices for petroleum products in Europe → Fuel costs could rise for German households and air travelers.
cells.b: After the Hormuz blockade, Saudi crude was piped to Yanbu through the East-West Pipeline and shipped on to Europe via the SUMED pipeline and Suez (World Oil, March 25, 2026), and in June 2026 the premium of European jet fuel over Brent was higher than usual (Inspenet, citing Reuters). Saudi crude, however, made up only 0.8 percent of Germany's crude imports in 2025 (Federal Statistical Office), so the volume reaching Germany is small, and the effect on German fuel prices could not be confirmed.

cells.m: Disruptions on the Suez leg, the shortest sea route between Asia and Europe → Higher container freight rates and delivery delays → German import prices and manufacturers' procurement could be affected.
cells.b: In July 2026, 1,340 ships transited the Suez Canal, up 27 percent from a year earlier (citing Bloomberg, September 8, 2026), but in late August transits were still 40 percent below their level before the Houthi attacks (Lloyd's List). The Drewry Shanghai–Rotterdam rate was $4,401 per 40-foot container on August 21. No change in German companies' delivery times or import prices could be confirmed.

cells.r: No hybrid pathway targeting Germans has been confirmed.
The Suez shipping problem itself has no nuclear channel.
The Suez shipping problem has no channel related to the movement of people.
No direct military threat from Libya to Germans has been confirmed.

cells.m: Renewed escalation of the east-west standoff in Libya → Disrupted crude production and exports → Reduced supplies of Libyan crude, which accounts for about one-seventh of Germany's crude imports, could push up German refining costs and fuel prices.
cells.b: According to Germany's Federal Statistical Office, Libya supplied 10.4 million metric tons (13.8 percent) of Germany's 75.7 million metric tons of crude imports in 2025, the third-largest source after Norway and the United States (Federal Statistical Office, March 2026). No export disruptions were reported after the drone attack on the Zawiya refinery in August 2026 (Al Jazeera, August 11), and a road map for unified elections was signed on August 30; the link is substantial, but no actual supply disruption has been observed.

cells.r: Apart from crude, Germany's trade and technology are not meaningfully connected to Libya's split (crude is covered in the Energy and food cell).
No hybrid activity from Libya targeting Germans has been confirmed.
Libya's split has no nuclear channel.
Arrivals from Libya are concentrated in Italy and Greece, and no data isolate the effect of Libya's split on subsequent secondary movement to Germany.
U.S. airstrikes and the civil war are taking place inside Somalia, and no link to Germans' safety has been confirmed.
Somalia does not supply energy or food to Germany.

The main causes of insecurity on the Gulf of Aden route are Houthi attacks and the Hormuz crisis, and no case has been confirmed in which this conflict alone changed freight rates or volumes for German cargo.
No cyber or information operations targeting Germans in connection with this conflict have been confirmed.
This conflict has no nuclear channel.
Statistics on asylum applications by Somalis in Germany and on returns in 2025–2026, and their trend (before and after the clashes in Mogadishu and al-Shabaab's expansion), would settle this.
The dispute over chip controls involves no military threat.
Chip controls are unrelated to energy and food supply.

cells.m: Amid U.S.-China export-control rivalry, the Netherlands takes control of Nexperia and China bans exports of Nexperia chips → Disrupted supplies of standard automotive chips → German car and parts plants could face production cuts and short-time work.
cells.b: When the Dutch government took control of Nexperia in September 2025, China blocked re-exports of Nexperia chips; Volkswagen warned of production stoppages, and Bosch applied for short-time work at its Salzgitter plant (Industriemagazin and eNCA, November 7, 2025). Some chip exports were approved in November 2025, but Nexperia said in July 2026 that the auto industry was still suffering from chip shortages and that it expected the major problems to be resolved by the end of the year (IO+, July 20, 2026).

cells.r: Measures such as State Council Decree No. 835 are public legal instruments covered under Trade and technology, and there are no data on hybrid activity targeting Germans.
The dispute over chip controls has no nuclear element.
No link has been confirmed by which the dispute over chip controls has caused population movement involving Germany.
The Cobasna ammunition depot and Russian troops sit near the Ukrainian border, and with no armed clashes since 1992, no military link to Germans has been confirmed.
Gas for Transnistria is a small volume bought on the European spot market, so no change in German gas bills or supply has been confirmed.
No effect of the Transnistria issue on Germany's trade or supply chains has been confirmed.
Russian influence operations have been confirmed inside Moldova, but no activity targeting Germans through Transnistria has been confirmed.
Transnistria has no nuclear channel (the Cobasna depot holds conventional ammunition).
There are no data showing any movement to Germany from Transnistria, where the conflict remains frozen.

cells.m: Britain's support for Ukraine → Activity by a Russian intelligence-gathering ship in waters near Britain and lasers aimed at Royal Air Force (RAF) aircraft monitoring it → Risks to the safety of British service personnel and a heavier burden of guarding undersea infrastructure
cells.b: Defense Secretary John Healey said on November 19, 2025, that the Russian intelligence-gathering ship Yantar was at the edge of British waters north of Scotland and had directed lasers at RAF pilots monitoring it, and warned that military options were ready (Reuters). How far this behavior is linked to the war in Ukraine is an inference by Clisa Geopolitics, so confidence is rated medium.

cells.r: Britain imports almost no Russian energy, and news reports attribute the 2026 rise in British fuel and electricity bills to the Iran war and the Hormuz blockade, so no change through this pathway has been confirmed.
Britain's trade with Russia had already shrunk sharply under sanctions since 2022, and no change in Britons' daily lives through this pathway has been confirmed in the past 12 months.

cells.m: Recruitment of local people by Russian military intelligence, targeting Britain as a supporter of Ukraine → Attempted sabotage inside Britain → Threats to the safety of facilities used by people in Britain and heightened insecurity
cells.b: On September 9, 2026, British prosecutors charged Joshua Cammidge, a 31-year-old British man, with assisting a foreign intelligence service after he allegedly received sabotage instructions from a person who appeared to be an agent of the GRU Volunteer Corps, which is controlled by Russia's military intelligence agency (GRU) (Al Jazeera).

cells.r: Russia's threatening nuclear rhetoric continues, but no change has been observed in the daily lives of Britons; this is the same link as in the Western, Central, and Eastern European cell and gets the same verdict.

cells.m: A drawn-out war → Extended permission to stay for Ukrainians in Britain on Ukraine visa schemes (24 more months under the UPE) → Demand for housing, schools, and welfare in British communities, and the cost of reception policies, could persist.
cells.b: In an impact assessment for changes to the Immigration Rules (HC 1619) on March 5, 2026, the U.K. Home Office said it would extend the Ukraine Permission Extension (UPE) scheme by 24 months from August 2026, and estimated that of about 230,000 people who had arrived through Homes for Ukraine and other schemes, about 170,000 (140,000–190,000) would still be in Britain when their permission expired. About 26 percent are under 18.

cells.m: Attacks by Iran and pro-Iranian forces in the Gulf and the eastern Mediterranean → Threats to RAF Akrotiri on Cyprus and to British facilities and areas where Britons live in the Gulf → Risks to the personal safety of British service members and Britons abroad
cells.b: On the night of March 1, 2026, an Iranian-made Shahed-type drone struck the runway at RAF Akrotiri, and families on the base were moved to nearby accommodation (damage was minor and no one was injured); Prime Minister Keir Starmer, responding to Iranian attacks on British interests in the Gulf, allowed the United States limited use of British bases (AP, March 2, 2026). Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper said about 300,000 British citizens were in the Gulf states Iran had attacked (March 2, 2026).

cells.m: Shipping through Hormuz blocked → Higher global oil prices and wholesale gas prices → Higher gasoline prices and a higher household energy price cap in Britain → Higher consumer prices in Britain
cells.b: The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said Britain's consumer price inflation was 3.5 percent in September 2026, the highest since October 2025, and that motor fuel prices had risen 30 percent over the year; the report cited the Iran war and the Hormuz bottleneck as causes (AP, October 21, 2026). The energy regulator Ofgem confirmed a 4 percent increase in the household price cap from October, citing higher wholesale gas prices caused by the conflict in the Middle East (BusinessGreen).

cells.r: The effect on Britons' daily lives comes through energy prices, and no separate link through trade or technology supply chains has been confirmed (the same verdict as the Western, Central, and Eastern European cell).

cells.m: Iranian state threats and activity by proxy groups suspected of links to Iran → Arson and surveillance targeting Jewish sites and Iranian dissidents in Britain, and cyberattacks on infrastructure → Risks to personal safety and anxiety in British communities
cells.b: On March 23, 2026, four ambulances belonging to Hatzola, a Jewish volunteer ambulance service, were burned in Golders Green, London, and police investigated a claim of responsibility by a group possibly linked to Iran (AP, March 25, 2026). Around the same time, Metropolitan Police Commissioner Mark Rowley called the rapid growth of Iranian state threats in recent years "grave" and cited 20 foiled plots, and in March two people were charged with surveilling Jews and Jewish sites for Iran (Jewish News, March 24, 2026). There is also a report that a small power plant in Britain was shut down for four days in July 2026 by an attack suspected to be the work of Iran-linked hackers, but no official attribution has been confirmed (SecurityWeek).

cells.r: The unverified status of Iran's 60 percent enriched uranium is a proliferation risk, but any short-term pathway to Britons' daily lives is vague.

cells.m: Iranian attacks in the Gulf and closed airspace → Britons in the Gulf stranded and evacuated on government charter flights → Anxiety over personal safety and travel costs for Britons abroad and their families
cells.b: After Iranian attacks closed the airspace of several Gulf countries, 102,000 people had registered their whereabouts with the Foreign Office by March 2, 2026 (Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper); by March 4 the number registered had grown to about 130,000, and the first government repatriation charter flight left Muscat, Oman (STV).

cells.m: Renewed war between Israel and Hezbollah → A drone from Lebanon attacks RAF Akrotiri on Cyprus → Risks to the personal safety of service members and families on the base, and evacuations
cells.b: On the night of March 1, 2026, a Shahed-type drone struck the runway at RAF Akrotiri, and families on the base were moved to nearby accommodation (AP, March 2, 2026); Cyprus's foreign minister said on March 8 that the attack had been launched from Lebanon. Lebanon's foreign minister said Hezbollah's activities went against the will of the Lebanese government and people (Arab News).

cells.r: Israel's offshore gas goes mainly to Egypt and Jordan, and no change in the cost of living in Britain from the fighting in Lebanon and Gaza has been confirmed (the energy-price pathway is covered under the Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz flashpoint).
There is policy debate over matters such as arms export restrictions, but no change in trade affecting Britons' daily lives has been confirmed.

Arson and surveillance targeting Jewish sites in Britain in 2026 are covered under the Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz flashpoint, because whether they were linked to Iran is at issue in police investigations and media reports. Data separating out cases in Britain over the past 12 months that stemmed from the Lebanon and Gaza fronts would settle this.
The Lebanon and Gaza fronts involve no pathway through the use of nuclear weapons or attacks on nuclear facilities.
Displaced Lebanese moved within Lebanon or to Syria, and there are no data showing an increase in arrivals in Britain.
No military pathway involving the deployment of British forces or Britons has been confirmed.
Gas from the Southern Gas Corridor goes to Bulgaria, Greece, Italy, and other countries, and no link to Britain's gas supply has been confirmed.
The Middle Corridor carries little freight and TRIPP has not yet broken ground, so no change in trade affecting Britons' daily lives has been confirmed.
No hybrid activity targeting Britain in this conflict has been confirmed.
None of the parties to the conflict has nuclear weapons, and there is no nuclear threat pathway.
Displaced people from Karabakh have settled in Armenia, and no flow of refugees or migrants toward Britain has been confirmed.

Since the al-Hol camp closed, the whereabouts of some former residents remain unknown, but nothing observed ties them to terrorist plots in Britain, so the concern remains general (the same verdict as the Western, Central, and Eastern European cell).
Syria is not a major supplier of energy or food, so this channel has no meaningful effect.
Trade and technology ties between Britain and Syria are small, so there is no meaningful effect.
No hybrid attack from Syria targeting Britain has been confirmed.
The Syrian conflict currently involves no nuclear pathway.

cells.m: Syria enters its transition → The British government considers resuming forced returns to Syria and discusses returns with the Syrian government → Uncertainty over the status of Syrian asylum seekers and refugees in Britain, and returns becoming a domestic political issue

Gas for Transnistria is a small volume bought on the European spot market, and no change in Britain's energy or food supply has been confirmed.
No effect of the Transnistria issue on Britain's trade or supply chains has been confirmed.
Russian influence operations have been confirmed inside Moldova, but no activity targeting Britain through Transnistria has been confirmed.
Transnistria has no nuclear channel (the Cobasna depot holds conventional ammunition).
There are no data showing any movement toward Britain from Transnistria, where the conflict remains frozen.

cells.m: North Korea's troop deployment to Russia and Russia-North Korea military cooperation → North Korean forces gain combat experience and improve their missile accuracy → North Korea's military threat to Japan could grow.
cells.b: In its 2026 defense white paper (reported in August 2026), Japan's Ministry of Defense assessed that North Korea had sent artillery shells, ballistic missiles, and troops to Russia and was gaining experience in drone warfare and improving its missile accuracy, and that Russia could transfer nuclear and missile technology in return.

cells.m: Sanctions on Russia and a drawn-out war → Uncertainty over shipping, insurance, and payment for the Sakhalin-2 LNG that Japan imports under long-term contracts → Gas and electricity supply and bills could come under pressure.
cells.b: On October 1, 2026, Britain issued a general license allowing imports into Japan and South Korea of Sakhalin-2 LNG under contracts concluded before June 17, 2025, until March 31, 2028 (S&P Global), and in its 21st sanctions package, adopted on July 23, the EU likewise decided not to apply restrictions on shipping, financial, and other services to Sakhalin-2 LNG bound for South Korea and Japan until the same deadline (The Asia Business Daily). In 2026, South Korea's and Japan's combined imports of Sakhalin-2 LNG come to about 4.8 million tons (about 5.9 percent of the two countries' LNG imports). Supply after the exemptions expire and the effect on Japanese bills could not be confirmed.

cells.r: Data on changes in Japan's exports to Russia over the past 12 months (Ministry of Finance trade statistics) and on losses and jobs at Japanese companies doing business in Russia would settle this.

cells.m: Japan's support for Ukraine → DDoS attacks by the pro-Russian hacker group NoName057(16) on Japanese local governments and transport and logistics bodies → Access to government and transport websites could be disrupted.
cells.b: In an analysis dated February 16, 2026, the security firm SOCRadar reported that the pro-Russian hacker group NoName057(16) carried out about 2,144 DDoS attacks on 44 Japanese organizations, including Aomori Airport, the Civil Aviation Bureau, and local governments, from February 9 to 15, 2026; in a September 7, 2026, report, Check Point said the group claimed 66 attacks on 26 Japanese organizations from August 24 to 30, citing Japan's support for Ukraine and NATO. Both analyses rely on the hacker group's own claims for the number of attacks, and neither confirmed actual service outages.

cells.r: Japan's Ministry of Defense assessed that Russia could transfer nuclear and missile technology to North Korea (2026 defense white paper), but no actual transfer has been publicly confirmed. A government statement confirming a transfer would settle this.

cells.m: Flight from the war → Long-term stays by Ukrainian evacuees accepted by the Japanese government → The burden on support budgets and on the local governments and communities where they have settled could continue.
cells.b: According to the Immigration Services Agency of Japan, 2,910 Ukrainian evacuees have entered Japan since March 2, 2022, and 1,922 were in the country as of October 31, 2026 (preliminary figures). The size of the burden on local governments and communities could not be confirmed.

cells.m: Attacks on merchant ships and transit controls in the Strait of Hormuz → Risk of attack on Japan-linked ships stranded in the Gulf and losses for shipping companies, and safety risks for Maritime Self-Defense Force personnel gathering intelligence in the Gulf of Oman and the northern Arabian Sea
cells.b: Ships owned by Mitsui O.S.K. Lines were damaged one after another, in the Gulf of Oman on March 4, 2026, and in Gulf waters about 100 km from the Strait of Hormuz on March 11 (Japanese-flagged; cause unknown; no casualties). As of a June 22 report, Japan-linked ships stranded in the Gulf had fallen from 45 at the start of the war to 37, and all 24 Japanese seafarers who were there when the war began had left. The Maritime Self-Defense Force's information-gathering mission in the Middle East began with a Cabinet decision in December 2019 and has been extended every year; according to the Joint Staff of the Ministry of Defense, under a Cabinet decision in November 2025, one destroyer and one patrol aircraft are carrying out this mission, along with counterpiracy operations, on the high seas of the Gulf of Oman and the northern Arabian Sea. The destroyer Takanami departed as the relief unit on June 6, 2026, and on November 6, 2026, the government extended the mission by one year, to November 19, 2027 (Kyodo News, November 6, 2026). No damage to the Japan Self-Defense Forces has been confirmed.

cells.m: Blocked transit through Hormuz → A surge in global oil prices and disrupted supplies of Middle Eastern crude → Higher gasoline prices, electricity bills, and consumer prices in Japan
cells.b: Japan began releasing oil from its national reserves on March 16, 2026. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi announced a plan for Japan to release 80 million barrels on its own, and that day Brent crude stood at $104.85 a barrel, up more than 40 percent since the war began on February 28 (Al Jazeera, March 16, 2026).

cells.m: Blockade of Hormuz → Disrupted supplies of naphtha from the Middle East → Production cuts at Japanese petrochemical plants and shortages of plastics and other materials
cells.b: The Japan Petrochemical Industry Association said on April 23 that ethylene plant utilization in March 2026 was 68.6 percent, the lowest since records began in January 1996. The low rate reflected production cuts made in anticipation of feedstock shortages, coinciding with scheduled maintenance; Japan imports about 40 percent of its naphtha from the Middle East.

cells.r: No data confirm Iranian cyber or covert operations against Japanese institutions or companies, or related terrorism in Japan, in connection with this war. When Handala, a hacker group assessed as linked to Iran's intelligence ministry, attacked the U.S. medical device maker Stryker on March 11, 2026, devices at its sites in Japan were also wiped (according to an NTT security report), but the target was a U.S. company.
The unverified stock of 60 percent enriched uranium is a proliferation risk, but there is no concrete near-term pathway to the daily lives of the Japanese public.

cells.m: Airstrikes and a widening war → Japanese in Iran, the Gulf, and Israel evacuate overland and return home on charter flights → Risks to the personal safety of Japanese residents and expatriate staff, and disrupted livelihoods
cells.b: Japan's Foreign Ministry said on March 8, 2026, that 188 Japanese nationals and their foreign-national family members had left Iran, the UAE, and Kuwait with government help (90 from the UAE to Muscat, Oman; 84 from Kuwait to Riyadh; and 14 from Tehran to Baku, Azerbaijan). Those who wished to return home flew into Narita on charter flights.

There is no military link to Japan, and even if border clashes resumed, there would be no pathway to the safety of the Japanese public.

Japan's trade through the Middle Corridor (the trans-Caspian route) is small and construction of the TRIPP corridor has not begun, so the pathway to the daily lives of the Japanese public is weak.
There is no pathway for cyber or information operations aimed at Japan.
None of the parties to the conflict has nuclear weapons, and there is no nuclear threat pathway.
Refugees from Karabakh have settled in Armenia, and no flow of refugees or migrants toward Japan, or related policy, has been confirmed.

The Japan Self-Defense Forces have no presence in Syria, and no pathway by which Israel's troop presence in southern Syria and its airstrikes threaten the safety of the Japanese public has been confirmed.

Japan's trade and technology ties with Syria are small, so there is no meaningful effect.

cells.m: A Taiwan contingency → The possibility that Japan exercises its right of collective self-defense, and the use of U.S. Forces Japan bases → Japan Self-Defense Forces personnel and residents of Okinawa and Japan's southwestern islands could be exposed to the risk of attack.
cells.b: In November 2025, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said, in effect, that Japan could intervene militarily if China tried to take Taiwan by force, and China, in protest, has kept up its pressure on Japan (AFP, February 18, 2026). Large-scale drills around Taiwan have now diminished, but gray-zone pressure has become routine.

cells.m: A blockade or the declaration of drill zones around Taiwan → Oil and LNG shipments bound for Japan through the Bashi Channel and east of Taiwan are rerouted → Freight rates and insurance premiums could rise.
cells.b: Japan's Institute of Geoeconomics (IOG), a think tank, found that Japan's crude and LNG shipping routes from the Middle East pass through the Strait of Malacca, the South China Sea, and the Bashi Channel between Taiwan and the Philippines (March 3, 2026), and one analysis held that the Justice Mission 2025 drills of December 29 and 30, 2025, rehearsed seizing control of the Bashi Channel and the Miyako Strait (Al Jazeera, December 30, 2025). No named large-scale drills have been held since then, and no disruption to merchant shipping has been observed, so the effect is weak.

cells.m: Rising tension in the Taiwan Strait → Possible disruption in supplies of advanced chips from Taiwan → Electronics and auto production in Japan that relies on Taiwanese chips could be affected.
cells.b: According to the U.S. Commerce Department's Country Commercial Guide (posted December 1, 2025), Taiwan accounts for more than 60 percent of global foundry revenue and more than 90 percent of leading-edge chip manufacturing. No actual supply disruption has been observed at the current level of gray-zone pressure, and the volume of Japan's chip imports from Taiwan could not be confirmed.

cells.r: Information operations against Japan related to Taiwan are covered in the East China Sea (China-Japan dispute) cell, and no data on operations against Japan stemming separately from the Taiwan Strait have been confirmed.
At the current level of gray-zone pressure, no pathway to nuclear use or nuclear threats has taken concrete shape.

cells.m: A Taiwan contingency → Under a government plan, about 120,000 residents and tourists evacuate from the Sakishima Islands toward Kyushu → Islanders are uprooted from their livelihoods, and the areas that take them in bear the burden
cells.b: In March 2025, the Japanese government released a plan to evacuate about 120,000 residents and tourists from five islands near Taiwan to Kyushu by ship and aircraft within six days in an "emergency" such as a Taiwan contingency. No actual evacuation has taken place at the current level of gray-zone pressure, and the plan is more than 12 months old.

cells.m: Frequent North Korean ballistic missile launches → Missiles fall into the East Sea (Sea of Japan) and fly irregular trajectories → Threats to the safety of ships, aircraft, and residents around Japan
cells.b: Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said on January 4, 2026, that North Korea had fired at least two ballistic missiles, which appeared to have landed in the East Sea outside Japan's exclusive economic zone (EEZ) and may have flown irregular trajectories, and he lodged a strong protest through Japan's embassy in Beijing. The Defense Ministry also announced that North Korean ballistic missiles were believed to have landed in the East Sea outside the EEZ on April 19 and August 20. No damage to ships or aircraft was reported.

cells.r: Current tensions on the Korean Peninsula do not affect Japan's energy and food import routes (this could change in a full-scale conflict).
No change in Japanese markets or trade linked to North Korea's 2026 missile launches has been confirmed, so there is no specific link beyond general arguments.

cells.m: Fake job interviews and malware from North Korean hackers → Theft of wallet data from Japanese developers and crypto users → Financial losses
cells.b: On September 18, 2026, Japan's National Police Agency, together with the United States, said that WaterPlum, a hacking group linked to Bureau 313 of North Korea's Workers' Party, had posed as recruiters to infect more than 30,000 computers in more than 100 countries and regions, including Japan, and steal more than 7,000 crypto wallet records, and that at least 1.7 billion yen had flowed into the group's wallets. The scale of losses by Japanese victims was not disclosed separately.

cells.m: North Korea expands its nuclear arsenal and diversifies its delivery systems → A growing threat of nuclear attack, with all of Japan and U.S. Forces Japan bases within range
cells.b: North Korea has fired at least 15 ballistic missiles in nine launches so far in 2026 and rejects denuclearization even as an agenda item, and Japan's Defense Ministry assessed in its 2026 defense white paper that Russia could transfer nuclear and missile technology to North Korea.

cells.r: Japan takes in very few North Korean defectors, and no link through population movement from North Korea's border controls to the daily lives of the Japanese public has been confirmed.

cells.m: Fire-control radar lock-ons by Chinese fighters, live-fire drills, and joint Chinese-Russian bomber flights → Risk of accidental clashes in the seas and airspace around Japan → Threats to the safety of Japan Self-Defense Forces personnel and residents
cells.b: According to Japan, J-15 fighters from the Chinese carrier Liaoning twice locked radar on Japanese aircraft near Okinawa in December 2025 (AFP, February 18, 2026). On June 27, 2026, Chinese H-6 and Russian Tu-95 bombers, among other aircraft, made a joint flight, prompting Japan's Air Self-Defense Force to scramble jets, and Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi criticized it as a show of force aimed at Japan (Stars and Stripes, June 29, 2026).

cells.r: No interference with merchant shipping bound for Japan in the East China Sea has been observed. China's suspension of Japanese seafood imports is a fisheries export issue and is covered in the Trade and technology cell.

cells.m: China's ban on exports of dual-use items and rare earths to Japan, and its advisory against travel to Japan → Disrupted supplies of materials for defense and manufacturing, and a sharp drop in Chinese tourists → Lower revenue for the companies involved and for tourism and retail
cells.b: On February 24, 2026, China's Commerce Ministry banned exports of dual-use items to 20 Japanese entities, including the shipbuilding and aircraft engine divisions of Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, and put 20 others, including Subaru, on a watch list. Visitors from mainland China in January 2026 numbered 385,300, down 60.7 percent from a year earlier, according to the Japan National Tourism Organization (China had advised its citizens on November 14, 2025, to avoid traveling to Japan). On September 8, 2026, China imposed provisional anti-dumping deposits of up to 99.2 percent on Japanese dichlorosilane (a material used in chipmaking) exported by Shin-Etsu Chemical and others, and the Japanese government protested (AP).

cells.m: The China-Japan dispute → Information operations using fake accounts aimed at Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Japanese politics → Attempts to interfere in Japanese elections and public opinion
cells.b: In an analysis reported on February 26, 2026, the U.S.-based Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD) said that 35 X accounts and nine Tumblr channels had attacked Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and spread corruption allegations, and that the network was likely part of a long-running Chinese operation (Spamouflage). Engagement was low, and the Chinese embassy dismissed the claims as groundless. OpenAI said in a February 2026 report that an official linked to Chinese law enforcement had asked ChatGPT in mid-October 2025 to draw up a plan to discredit Takaichi and had been refused (Jiji Press, February 27, 2026).

The drop in Chinese tourists runs through tourism (trade in services) and is covered in the Trade and technology cell. The tariffs on Mexico tied to the cartel problem were repealed on February 24, 2026, so there is currently no link through this channel to Japanese companies with production bases in Mexico or to the Japanese public.

cells.m: Mexican authorities' operation that killed cartel boss "El Mencho" → Road blockades, arson, and clashes between authorities and criminal groups in Jalisco, Guanajuato, and elsewhere → Risks to the personal safety of Japanese in these areas and limits on their movement
cells.b: On February 23, 2026, Japan's Foreign Ministry said that Mexico's Defense Ministry had carried out an operation against the Jalisco New Generation Cartel (CJNG) in the state of Jalisco in which its leader, Nemesio Oseguera ("El Mencho"), was killed, and that highway blockades and arson attacks were continuing across a wide area including Jalisco, Guanajuato, and Aguascalientes; it urged Japanese in the country to avoid nonessential outings. The announcement did not confirm any harm to Japanese nationals.

cells.r: The cartel and border problem has no nuclear pathway.
Migration controls at the U.S.-Mexico border have no link to migration toward Japan or Japan's border controls.
The port dispute is being pursued through legal and commercial means, and no threat of force has been found.
The canal itself is operating without disruption, so no effect on energy and grain shipments to Japan through the Panama Canal has been confirmed.

Detentions of Panama-flagged ships at Chinese ports rose into the 90s in March 2026 and into the 130s in each of April and May (according to reports citing Tokyo MOU data); data on how many of these ships are beneficially owned by Japanese shipowners, the cost of the detentions, and how many ships Japanese shipowners have reflagged would settle this.
No hybrid activity aimed at Japan has been confirmed in connection with the Panama port dispute.
The Panama port dispute has no nuclear channel.
The dispute over port operating rights has no pathway related to refugee flows, migration, or border controls.

No deployment of the Japan Self-Defense Forces to the UN Gang Suppression Force (GSF) has been confirmed, and there is no pathway from gang violence in Haiti to the physical safety of the Japanese public.
The Haiti crisis has no pathway related to Japan's energy and food supply.
Japan's trade with Haiti is small, so no link to the daily lives of the Japanese public has been confirmed.
Gun trafficking and kidnappings by Haitian gangs are confined to the Americas, and no pathway to Japan has been confirmed.
The Haiti crisis has no nuclear pathway.
Displacement and returns of Haitians take place within the Americas, and no flow toward Japan has been confirmed.
A trade war between allies has no military threat pathway.
The U.S. ban on imports of Canadian dairy products and alcohol is a matter for the U.S. market, and no case of it changing Japan's energy and food supply has been confirmed.

The tariffs the U.S. and Canada have imposed on each other could affect the earnings of Japanese companies with plants in Canada, but the effect stays at the corporate level, and no resulting change in employment or prices in Japan has been observed.
No hybrid activity aimed at Japan has been confirmed in connection with the U.S.-Canada dispute.
The trade war has no nuclear pathway.
The U.S.-Canada dispute has no link to migration toward Japan or Japan's border controls.
No military pathway from the ground strikes in Ecuador's border areas and the state of emergency to the physical safety of the Japanese public has been confirmed.
No case has been confirmed of gang violence disrupting Japan's food imports from Ecuador.
Gang extortion and the state of emergency have had no observed effect on Japanese companies or consumers.
Cocaine trafficked through Ecuadorian ports goes mainly to the Americas and Europe, and no distribution route leading to Japan has been confirmed.
Ecuador's gang violence has no nuclear channel.
Ecuadorian migration heads elsewhere in the Americas, and no flow toward Japan has been confirmed.

Japan evacuated its nationals from Sudan on Japan Self-Defense Forces aircraft in April 2023, and there are no data showing any Japanese nationals in the current combat zones (Kordofan and Blue Nile), so no military pathway has been confirmed.
Sudan's civil war has no pathway related to Japan's energy and food supply.
Japan's trade with Sudan is small, so no link to the daily lives of the Japanese public has been confirmed.
No activity aimed at Japan, and no criminal pathway leading to Japan, has been confirmed in the weapons and drone supply chains of Sudan's civil war.
Sudan's civil war has no nuclear pathway.
Sudanese refugees head to neighboring countries such as Chad, Egypt, and Ethiopia, and no flow toward Japan has been confirmed.

The insurgent offensive in the Sahel is an internal matter for Mali, Burkina Faso, and Niger, and no military pathway related to the Japanese public or the Japan Self-Defense Forces has been confirmed.
The fuel blockade of Bamako has no pathway related to Japan's energy and food supply.
Attacks on supply routes in the Sahel have had no observed effect on Japan's trade or the daily lives of the Japanese public.
No hybrid activity aimed at Japan, and no criminal pathway leading to Japan, has been confirmed in the Sahel.
No pathway from this conflict to Japan's nuclear safety, including through Niger's uranium, has been confirmed.
Refugees from the Sahel head to neighboring countries and Europe, and no flow toward Japan has been confirmed.
No military pathway linking the fighting in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo to the Japanese public or the Japan Self-Defense Forces has been confirmed.
The conflict in eastern Congo has no pathway related to Japan's energy and food supply.
No effect of M23's seizure of mining areas on Japanese companies' mineral sourcing or on product prices in Japan has been confirmed, so the case remains a general argument.
No concrete pathway by which conflict minerals smuggled out of the region reach Japan has been confirmed.
The conflict in eastern Congo has no nuclear pathway.
Refugees from eastern Congo head to neighboring countries such as Burundi and Uganda, and no flow toward Japan has been confirmed.

On September 26, 2026, Japan's Foreign Ministry kept its advisory against travel to most of Tigray and its evacuation advisory for the west and the areas bordering Eritrea, urging caution, but no harm to Japanese nationals has been confirmed, and there are no reports of any threat to the Japan Self-Defense Forces base in neighboring Djibouti, so the cell is rated not connected, the same as the cell for South Koreans.
The Tigray war has no pathway related to Japan's energy and food supply.
Japan's trade with Ethiopia and Eritrea is small, so no link to the daily lives of the Japanese public has been confirmed.
Suspected Eritrean support for rebels is a matter of regional proxy war, and no activity aimed at Japan has been confirmed.
The Tigray war has no nuclear pathway.
People displaced from Tigray and Amhara remain within the country or in neighboring countries, and no flow toward Japan has been confirmed.

cells.m: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and shipping risks in the Bab el-Mandeb → Safety risks for Japan Self-Defense Forces personnel based in Djibouti on counter-piracy duty in the adjacent Gulf of Aden and for Japanese living in Saudi Arabia
cells.b: From their base in the northwest zone of Djibouti International Airport, the Japan Self-Defense Forces continue surveillance of the Gulf of Aden with P-3C patrol aircraft and are still rotating units in 2026 (Japan's Joint Staff), and in September 2026 Houthi attacks reached Aramco facilities in Abha, Najran, and Jizan and the air base at Khamis Mushait (AGBI). No harm to the SDF or to Japanese nationals has been confirmed, so confidence is rated low.

cells.m: Houthi attacks effectively close Bab el-Mandeb to Saudi crude shipments → Crude sent to Yanbu to avoid Hormuz is rerouted via Suez and the Cape of Good Hope (voyages lengthen from about 20 days to 50–60 days) → Higher shipping costs for Japanese refiners and the burden of gasoline and electricity bills
cells.b: According to Reuters (August 18, 2026), Japan imported 94 percent of its crude from the Middle East in 2025, 93 percent of which passed through Hormuz, and after Houthi attacks made the Bab el-Mandeb impassable for most Saudi crude shipments, Idemitsu Kosan began bringing in crude loaded at Yanbu via Suez and the Cape of Good Hope, lengthening a voyage of about 20 days to 50 to 60 days. Crude buyers at two Japanese refiners said in mid-July that 2 million to 5 million barrels a month of Arab Light could be brought in via the Red Sea route (S&P Global Platts, July 16, 2026). The size of the effect on consumer prices could not be confirmed.

cells.m: Shipping risks in the Bab el-Mandeb → ONE, the container line set up by Japan's three major shipping companies, and others divert Asia–Europe services around the Cape of Good Hope → Longer voyages and higher freight rates → Higher logistics costs for Japanese importers and exporters
cells.b: ONE switched its Asia–Europe services to the Cape of Good Hope route, citing security risks in the Red Sea region (India Seatrade News, May 29, 2026), and as of September 2026 many container ships were still diverting around the Cape of Good Hope (AGBI). The size of the effect on Japanese importers' and exporters' logistics costs could not be confirmed.

cells.r: The seizure of a ship operated by a Japanese shipping company (the Galaxy Leader) in November 2023 falls outside the past 12 months, and no hybrid activity aimed at Japan has been confirmed in this conflict.
The Red Sea front has no nuclear channel.
Yemeni refugees stay within the country or head to Djibouti and elsewhere, and no flow toward Japan has been confirmed.

No pathway has been confirmed by which threats to Egyptian ports, such as the drone attack on the port of Damietta, affect the physical safety of the Japanese public (risks to individual seafarers are a separate matter).

cells.m: Saudi crude from Yanbu, routed away from the Bab el-Mandeb, reaches Japan via Suez and the SUMED pipeline → Attacks on tankers using this route and threats to Egyptian ports → Risk of disrupted crude supplies and higher shipping costs for Japanese refiners
cells.b: Idemitsu Kosan began bringing in Saudi crude loaded at Yanbu via the Suez route in August 2026, and Saudi Aramco had been offering cargoes loaded at Sidi Kerir in Egypt since July (Reuters, August 18, 2026). On August 24, a Saudi tanker shuttling between Ain Sokhna and Yanbu was hit, exposing this detour to threats as well (AGBI). The share of Japan's crude imports that passes through Suez could not be confirmed.

cells.m: Threats to the Suez and Red Sea stretch, the shortest sea route between Asia and Europe → Japanese carrier ONE and others divert around the Cape of Good Hope, and freight rates rise → Higher logistics costs for Japanese importers and exporters and higher import prices
cells.b: According to Lloyd's List Intelligence, Suez transits in the four weeks to August 23, 2026, were the highest since February 2024 but 40 percent below the same period before the Houthi attacks, and shipping lines' decisions to return remain tentative. ONE switched its Asia–Europe services to the Cape of Good Hope route in May (India Seatrade News, May 29, 2026). The size of the effect on Japanese companies' logistics costs could not be confirmed.

cells.r: No hybrid pathway aimed at Japan has been confirmed in connection with the Suez Canal issue.
The Suez shipping problem itself has no nuclear channel.
The Suez shipping problem has no channel related to the movement of people.
No military pathway linking the east-west standoff in Libya to the Japanese public or the Japan Self-Defense Forces has been confirmed.
Libya accounts for a small share of Japan's crude imports, so no effect of attacks on oil facilities on Japan's energy supply has been confirmed.
Delays in Libya's reconstruction projects have had no observed effect on the daily lives of the Japanese public.
Outside powers' backing of Libyan factions is not aimed at Japan, and migrant smuggling routes also head toward the Mediterranean.
Libya's split has no nuclear pathway.
Sea migration via Libya heads to Europe, and no flow toward Japan has been confirmed.

The Japan Self-Defense Forces continue counter-piracy operations off Somalia from their base in Djibouti, but no link between the resurgence of piracy in 2026 and this conflict (the dispute over recognition of Somaliland and the clashes in Mogadishu), and no harm to Japan-linked ships or the SDF, has been confirmed.
The conflict in Somalia has no pathway related to Japan's energy and food supply.

Instability on Gulf of Aden routes stems mainly from Houthi attacks from Yemen and the Hormuz crisis, and no case has been confirmed of this conflict alone changing Japan's freight rates or cargo volumes.
Somali piracy rose again in 2026, but no harm to Japan-linked ships has been confirmed, and no evidence has been found that the resurgence of piracy stems from Somalia's internal conflict.
The conflict in Somalia has no nuclear pathway.
Somalis displaced by the conflict remain within the country or in neighboring countries, and no flow toward Japan has been confirmed.
The dispute over chip controls involves no military threat.
Chip controls are unrelated to Japan's energy and food supply.

cells.m: U.S. controls on chip equipment exports to China and pressure on allies to align their controls, along with China's push to localize equipment and its countermeasure laws → Lower China sales and business constraints for Tokyo Electron and other Japanese equipment makers → Exports and jobs in Japan's chip equipment industry could be affected.
cells.b: According to a report citing a Nikkei tally, China sales by five companies (Tokyo Electron, Advantest, Screen Holdings, Disco, and Kokusai Electric) fell for the first time in fiscal 2025 (the year ended March 2026), to 1.47 trillion yen, and those of the three front-end equipment makers fell by nearly 20 percent (TrendForce, June 22, 2026). China accounted for 34.1 percent of Tokyo Electron's revenue in the same fiscal year, and the MATCH Act, which would align U.S., Dutch, and Japanese equipment controls and require licenses even for maintenance, is pending in Congress (TrendForce DataTrack, July 2026). China's localization of equipment also contributed to the decline, so the share due to U.S. controls alone cannot be isolated.

cells.r: Measures such as State Council Decree No. 835 are publicly enacted legal tools and are covered in the Trade and technology cell; there are no data on hybrid activity aimed at Japan in this dispute.
The dispute over chip controls has no nuclear element.

No data have been found showing that chip controls reduced the number of Japanese staff posted in China or prompted technical personnel to relocate, so there is no link to migration or border controls.
Russian troops in Transnistria and the risk posed by the Cobasna ammunition depot are an issue for the Moldovan-Ukrainian border area, and there is no pathway related to the Japanese public.
The gas supply problem in Transnistria is unrelated to Japan's energy supply.
No trade pathway between Transnistria and Japan has been confirmed.
Russia's expanded granting of citizenship targets Moldova and is not aimed at Japan.
The frozen conflict has no nuclear pathway.
Citizenship and movement issues for Transnistria's residents are unrelated to flows toward Japan.
